subject: Architecture
title: Outrigger Trusses: Hidden Strength
description: One-minute skill: Outrigger Trusses: Hidden Strength.

hook.text: Inside many supertall towers, massive hidden trusses connect the core to the exterior columns.

buildup.text: Outrigger trusses work like a person spreading their arms for balance — they widen the tower's stance.

discovery.text: The trusses are often two stories tall and occupy mechanical floors, hidden from office workers below.

twist.text: Without outriggers, the Burj Khalifa would need 60% more concrete to resist the same wind forces.

climax.text: Outrigger systems let engineers build taller with less material — efficiency enabling record heights.

punchline.text: The strongest parts of a skyscraper are the ones nobody sees.

quiz.question: What do outrigger trusses do in a supertall building?
options: They channel rainwater from the roof to the ground
They connect the core to exterior columns for wind resistance
They support the elevator machinery at the top

details.summary: Outrigger trusses are massive horizontal structures connecting a skyscraper's core to its perimeter columns, typically hidden on mechanical floors. They dramatically increase a building's stiffness against wind by engaging exterior columns as structural braces, reducing sway and material costs.
details.whyItMatters: Outriggers are the invisible trick behind many of the world's tallest buildings. They allow engineers to build taller with less material by efficiently distributing forces that would otherwise concentrate in the core alone.
takeaways: Outriggers connect the core to perimeter columns horizontally
They dramatically increase stiffness against wind forces
Hidden on mechanical floors, they reduce sway and material use

faq.question: Where are outrigger trusses located in a building?
faq.answer: Typically on mechanical floors — levels dedicated to HVAC equipment, elevator machinery, and building services. These floors have no rental value, so placing massive trusses there does not sacrifice usable space. Most supertalls have outriggers at two or three levels.

faq.question: How much do outriggers help reduce building sway?
faq.answer: A well-placed pair of outrigger trusses can reduce lateral deflection by 25-40% compared to a core-only structure. This means the building can be taller with the same amount of structural material, or uses less material to achieve the same height.
